stocks.summary: Structural Growth สูงจาก AI/Data Center และ Power Electronics แต่ต้องระวัง Valuation ที่สูงมาก ซึ่งทำให้ Margin of Safety ต่ำ

framework.1. Management: Global Delta ecosystem; strong engineering and manufacturing execution. Minority investors remain exposed to parent-group strategic priorities.
framework.2. Product / Moat: Power management and electronic components for data center, industrial and EV applications. Engineering know-how, qualification, scale and global customer relationships create a strong moat.
framework.3. TAM / Growth Runway: Structural exposure to AI/data-center power infrastructure, high-efficiency power conversion and EV. Growth runway is strong, but market expectations are already high.
framework.4. Positive Catalysts: AI/data-center power demand; margin expansion; regional manufacturing growth; EV and industrial automation.
framework.5. Competitors: Vertiv, Schneider, Eaton and Asian power-supply manufacturers.
framework.6. Revenue Growth & Margin: Growth and margin expansion are occurring together; the operating profile is excellent.
framework.7. Regulation: Main risk is global trade/geopolitical policy: tariffs, export controls, local-content rules and supply-chain fragmentation.
framework.8. Narrative & Sentiment: AI infrastructure / data-center power winner; positive sentiment, but the equity story is no longer early-stage.
framework.9. Valuation Effect: Exceptional business quality is offset by an extreme starting multiple. Multiple compression is a material risk.
framework.10. Earnings & Macro: 1H2026 profit rose sharply YoY. Base case assumes continued earnings growth but lower equity upside because valuation is demanding.
framework.11. Risk Radar: Valuation; AI capex cycle; customer concentration; FX; geopolitics / supply chain.

stocks.thesis: High-quality structural-growth compounder with strong moat and balance sheet.
stocks.bear: Even strong earnings growth may not offset valuation compression if AI expectations normalize.
stocks.marketBelieves: AI/data-center demand can sustain premium growth for years.
stocks.marketMissing: The operating thesis can be right while the stock return disappoints because the entry multiple is extreme.
stocks.variables: AI capex, order growth, gross margin, customer mix, capex and P/E de-rating.
stocks.fit: Growth investor with high tolerance for valuation risk.
stocks.moatReason: มี Moat จาก Engineering Know-how, Customer Qualification, Scale, ความสัมพันธ์กับลูกค้าระดับโลก และการอยู่ใน Supply Chain ของ Delta Group ซึ่งทำให้การเปลี่ยน Supplier มีต้นทุนและความเสี่ยงต่อผู้ซื้อ
stocks.industryComparison: เปรียบเทียบกับอุตสาหกรรม Electronic Components / Power Electronics โดยเน้น Growth, Margin, ROIC, Balance Sheet และ Valuation เทียบผู้เล่น Global Power Management

stocks.debtEbitdaNote: Total Interest Bearing Debt / EBITDA, 6M/2026 (TTM-adjusted by SET)
stocks.summary: จุดเด่นคือ Value, Dividend, Asset Backing และคุณภาพเครดิต ขณะที่ Growth มีลักษณะ Cyclical และขึ้นกับ Commodity/บริษัทย่อย

framework.1. Management: State-controlled strategic energy company. Access to capital and strategic importance are strengths; minority-shareholder alignment can be affected by policy objectives.
framework.2. Product / Moat: Integrated energy infrastructure with gas, trading and major listed subsidiaries. Scale, infrastructure and strategic national role create a durable barrier.
framework.3. TAM / Growth Runway: Mature domestic platform. Growth depends on the energy cycle, subsidiaries, infrastructure, portfolio restructuring and new-energy investment.
framework.4. Positive Catalysts: Oil/gas cycle; subsidiary recovery; petrochemical/refining normalization; portfolio restructuring; dividends.
framework.5. Competitors: Few true like-for-like peers because PTT is an integrated group; vertical integration and funding access are key advantages.
framework.6. Revenue Growth & Margin: Earnings are driven by commodity prices, refining/petrochemical spreads, inventory effects, FX and subsidiary profit.
framework.7. Regulation: Energy-price policy is both a barrier and a risk; policy can shift value among PTT, the state and consumers.
framework.8. Narrative & Sentiment: Cheap integrated energy conglomerate with dividend support and a persistent state/conglomerate discount.
framework.9. Valuation Effect: Low headline multiples and asset backing provide support, but re-rating may remain constrained by policy and conglomerate discount.
framework.10. Earnings & Macro: 1H2026 attributable profit increased strongly YoY. Macro sensitivity remains tied to oil, gas and downstream spreads.
framework.11. Risk Radar: Commodity cycle; government policy; petrochemical oversupply; capital allocation; energy transition.

stocks.thesis: Value, dividend and asset-backing case with strong funding access.
stocks.bear: Cheap valuation may persist if downstream returns stay weak or state-policy burden rises.
stocks.marketBelieves: PTT is mature, cyclical and deserves a state/conglomerate discount.
stocks.marketMissing: Subsidiary recovery and asset monetization can improve cash returns without requiring a high-growth narrative.
stocks.variables: Oil/gas prices, refining/petrochemical spreads, PTTEP earnings, dividends, capex and policy intervention.
stocks.moatReason: มี Moat จากโครงสร้างพื้นฐานพลังงานขนาดใหญ่ ระบบท่อและก๊าซ Scale, Vertical Integration และบทบาทเชิงยุทธศาสตร์ของประเทศ ซึ่งสร้าง Barrier to Entry สูง
stocks.industryComparison: เปรียบเทียบกับ Integrated Energy / Oil & Gas peers โดยเน้น EV/EBITDA, P/BV, Dividend, Commodity sensitivity และ Balance Sheet

stocks.debtEbitdaNote: Total Interest Bearing Debt / EBITDA, 6M/2026 (TTM-adjusted by SET)
stocks.summary: มี Business Quality, Moat, Cash Flow และ Earnings Visibility แข็งแรง Valuation อยู่ในระดับที่ต้องติดตามเทียบกับ Telecom peers

framework.1. Management: Strong historical execution with strategic shareholders GULF and Singtel. Capital discipline and operating track record are key strengths.
framework.2. Product / Moat: Mobile, fixed broadband, enterprise and digital services. Spectrum, network scale, subscriber base, switching friction and distribution create a strong moat.
framework.3. TAM / Growth Runway: Core mobile is mature, but 5G monetization, broadband, enterprise, cloud, data center, AI and digital-finance optionality extend the growth runway.
framework.4. Positive Catalysts: ARPU recovery; rational competition; broadband synergy; enterprise/cloud growth; operating leverage.
framework.5. Competitors: TRUE is the principal direct telecom peer. ADVANC currently has stronger profitability, balance-sheet quality and execution visibility.
framework.6. Revenue Growth & Margin: A quality-compounder pattern: moderate service-revenue growth, high margins, disciplined capex and strong cash generation.
framework.7. Regulation: NBTC spectrum, tariff, competition and service-quality regulation are both entry barriers and return-on-capital risks.
framework.8. Narrative & Sentiment: Thai telecom cash-flow compounder; positive sentiment supported by earnings growth and market structure.
framework.9. Valuation Effect: Not cheap, but substantially more reasonable than extreme-growth names. Earnings growth can still drive returns without aggressive re-rating.
framework.10. Earnings & Macro: 1H2026 attributable profit grew materially YoY. Telecom is relatively defensive, while ARPU and spectrum economics remain key variables.
framework.11. Risk Radar: Renewed price competition; spectrum cost; capex cycle; regulation; returns on new digital ventures.

stocks.thesis: Best balance of quality, moat, growth, cash flow and valuation in Batch 1.
stocks.bear: A return of aggressive price competition or expensive spectrum can reduce ROIC and cash-return capacity.
stocks.marketBelieves: Defensive telecom leader with improving earnings.
stocks.marketMissing: Enterprise/cloud and operating leverage may add more growth than a traditional telecom multiple implies.
stocks.variables: ARPU, churn, service revenue, EBITDA margin, capex, spectrum payments, FCF and dividend payout.
stocks.fit: Core quality/compounder investor and credit investor.
stocks.moatReason: มี Moat จาก Spectrum, Network Scale, ฐานลูกค้าขนาดใหญ่, Distribution, Switching Friction และโครงสร้างตลาดที่ต้องใช้เงินลงทุนสูง ทำให้ผู้เล่นใหม่เข้ามาแข่งขันได้ยาก
stocks.industryComparison: เปรียบเทียบกับ Telecom peers โดยเน้น ARPU, Churn, EBITDA Margin, Capex/Sales, FCF, Spectrum Cost และ Leverage

stocks.debtEbitdaNote: Total Interest Bearing Debt / EBITDA, 6M/2026 (TTM-adjusted by SET)
stocks.summary: มี Growth Optionality จาก Energy, ADVANC, Data Center และ Cloud แต่ต้องติดตาม Leverage, Funding Cost และ ROIC ของโครงการใหม่

framework.1. Management: Founder-led capital allocation with high ownership alignment. Complexity and leverage require close monitoring as the platform expands.
framework.2. Product / Moat: Energy, infrastructure, telecom exposure through ADVANC, data center/cloud and investments. Ecosystem breadth is difficult for a local peer to replicate.
framework.3. TAM / Growth Runway: Power and infrastructure remain core, while data center/cloud create a new structural growth leg.
framework.4. Positive Catalysts: ADVANC earnings; new power capacity; data centers; cloud/AI infrastructure; renewable projects; infrastructure investments.
framework.5. Competitors: Energy peers include GPSC, EGCO, RATCH and BGRIM, but no Thai peer has exactly the same energy-telecom-data ecosystem.
framework.6. Revenue Growth & Margin: Core profit and EBITDA are more useful than headline P/E because amalgamation-related one-offs distort reported comparisons.
framework.7. Regulation: Exposed to electricity, PPA, telecom, data/privacy, cloud and digital-finance regulation.
framework.8. Narrative & Sentiment: Thailand infrastructure-tech conglomerate rather than a traditional power stock.
framework.9. Valuation Effect: Headline P/E can be misleading due to amalgamation effects; SOTP is the preferred framework.
framework.10. Earnings & Macro: Q2 core profit and EBITDA were strong. Reported YoY net-profit comparisons are distorted by the 2025 amalgamation gain.
framework.11. Risk Radar: Leverage; execution across multiple businesses; regulation; capital allocation; data-center overbuild.

stocks.thesis: High-growth infrastructure platform with strategic telecom and data-center optionality.
stocks.bear: Complexity, leverage and large capital commitments can reduce returns if new projects earn below expected ROIC.
stocks.marketBelieves: GULF is evolving into a broad infrastructure holding company.
stocks.marketMissing: Data-center/cloud economics could become a more meaningful earnings leg than currently assumed.
stocks.variables: Core profit, ADVANC contribution, net debt, project COD, data-center MW contracted, funding cost and SOTP discount.
stocks.fit: Growth/infrastructure investor comfortable with leverage and complexity.
stocks.moatReason: มี Moat จาก Scale, Long-term Infrastructure/PPA assets, ความสามารถเข้าถึงเงินทุนและโครงการขนาดใหญ่ รวมถึง Strategic Ecosystem ใน Energy–Telecom–Data แต่ต้องติดตามว่าการขยายธุรกิจใหม่จะสร้าง ROIC ได้ยั่งยืนเพียงใด
stocks.industryComparison: เปรียบเทียบกับ Energy & Utilities / Infrastructure peers โดยเน้น Core Profit, ROIC, Net Debt, PPA quality, Funding Cost และ SOTP

stocks.debtEbitdaNote: คำนวณจากหนี้ที่มีภาระดอกเบี้ยในงบ 9M/FY2026 หาร SET EBITDA 29,108.74 ล้านบาท
stocks.summary: มี Natural Monopoly Moat ชัดเจนจากสนามบินหลักของประเทศ แต่ราคาหุ้นสะท้อน Premium Valuation และต้องอาศัย Passenger/Commercial Growth ต่อเนื่อง

framework.1. Management: State-controlled airport operator. Strategic infrastructure quality is high, while policy and concession decisions remain important.
framework.2. Product / Moat: Major Thai airport network with location-based natural-monopoly characteristics, regulated concessions and airline-route network effects.
framework.3. TAM / Growth Runway: Growth linked to international arrivals, airport capacity, commercial revenue, passenger charges and Thailand's hub strategy.
framework.4. Positive Catalysts: Tourism recovery; passenger growth; airport capacity expansion; non-aeronautical revenue; concession economics.
framework.5. Competitors: Minimal direct domestic competition for the same locations; competitive benchmark is other regional aviation hubs.
framework.6. Revenue Growth & Margin: Passenger growth provides operating leverage, but earnings growth must be judged against a premium starting valuation.
framework.7. Regulation: Passenger charges, concessions, airport fees, capacity investment and commercial contracts are policy-sensitive.
framework.9. Valuation Effect: The market pays a substantial premium for monopoly quality. Upside requires sustained passenger and commercial growth.
framework.10. Earnings & Macro: 9M FY2026 profit grew modestly YoY; tourism, airline capacity and concession terms are central drivers.
framework.11. Risk Radar: Tourism shock; concession/regulatory change; government influence; large capex; valuation.

stocks.thesis: One of the strongest moats in SET100 with long-duration aviation infrastructure value.
stocks.bear: Premium valuation can compress if tourism or commercial revenue grows slower than expected.
stocks.marketBelieves: AOT deserves a premium as Thailand's airport monopoly and tourism proxy.
stocks.marketMissing: The moat is exceptional, but high valuation leaves limited room for execution disappointment.
stocks.variables: International passengers, Chinese arrivals, aero/non-aero revenue, concession terms, capex and P/E.
stocks.fit: Quality infrastructure investor willing to pay a premium.
stocks.moatReason: มี Moat ชัดเจนจาก Location และสิทธิบริหารสนามบินหลักของประเทศ ลักษณะ Natural Monopoly, Regulation และ Network Effect ของสายการบิน ทำให้การสร้างคู่แข่งทดแทนทำได้ยากมาก
stocks.industryComparison: เปรียบเทียบกับ Airport Operators / Transportation Infrastructure peers โดยเน้น Passenger Growth, Aero/Non-aero Revenue, EBITDA Margin, Capex และ Valuation

stocks.debtEbitdaNote: NPL 2.92%; Coverage 205%; ROE ~10.5%; use capital/asset-quality metrics instead.
stocks.summary: กำไรและคุณภาพสินทรัพย์ดีขึ้นชัด แต่ราคาหุ้นได้ re-rate ไปมากแล้ว จุดต่อไปต้องพิสูจน์ว่า Fee/Digital/Cost Efficiency ชดเชย NIM ขาลงได้ต่อเนื่อง.

framework.1. Management: State-linked bank with strong strategic role in public-sector payment/digital infrastructure. Management under Payong Srivanich has improved profitability, efficiency and asset quality while scaling digital ecosystems. Capital allocation is conservative; alignment is strong on stability and dividends, though state-linked objectives can influence strategy.
framework.2. Product / Moat: Universal bank serving government, corporate, SME and retail customers. Moat comes from government ecosystem integration, Paotang/Krungthai NEXT scale, deposits and nationwide distribution. Moat: มี — especially data/distribution and public-sector rails; durability high while digital engagement stays active.
framework.3. TAM / Growth Runway: Thai banking TAM is mature, so runway comes from fee income, wealth, digital monetization, government-payment ecosystem and selective quality lending rather than rapid loan growth.
framework.4. Positive Catalysts: Fee/wealth growth; digital monetization; operating efficiency; lower credit cost; dividend; potential policy-driven transaction volumes. Probability medium-high / impact medium over 6-24 months.
framework.5. Competitors: Compare only with Thai large-bank industry on ROE, NIM, NPL, coverage, CAR and P/BV. Competitive edge is public-sector ecosystem and digital reach; risk is lower pricing flexibility around policy objectives.
framework.6. Revenue Growth & Margin: 1H26 profit grew 7.6% YoY despite NII pressure. Revenue mix is shifting toward non-interest income while cost/income improved. Margin expansion depends more on fees, productivity and credit cost than NIM.
framework.7. Regulation: BOT capital/liquidity/consumer-protection rules and government policy are key. Beginner: regulation limits risk-taking. Technical: it constrains leverage/pricing but raises barriers to entry and supports funding confidence.
framework.8. Narrative & Sentiment: Narrative is 'high-quality state-linked bank + digital platform + dividend'. Sentiment positive but re-rating has already occurred. Story is middle stage rather than beginning.
framework.9. Valuation Effect: At ~1.3x P/BV and ~11.8x P/E, valuation is no longer deep value. Expected return should come mainly from earnings/dividend; multiple expansion is less likely than earlier in the cycle.
framework.10. Earnings & Macro: 1H26 NPAT ~THB24.6bn, +7.6% YoY; Q2 NPAT THB12.1bn. NPL 2.92%, coverage 205%, NIM ~2.45%. Low Thai rates pressure NIM, but weak growth also supports benign funding costs. Base: resilient earnings; Bull: fee/credit-cost upside; Bear: NIM/asset-quality pressure.
framework.11. Risk Radar: Top risks: NIM compression (high probability/medium impact), Thai weak growth and household debt (medium/high), policy influence (medium/medium), credit normalization (medium/high). Monitor NIM, NPL, coverage, fee income and credit cost.

stocks.thesis: Strong franchise with public-sector digital ecosystem, improving efficiency and high reserve coverage; attractive for income/quality exposure rather than rapid growth.
stocks.bear: Re-rating has already lifted P/BV; falling rates can compress NIM faster than fees grow, while state-linked objectives may constrain pure shareholder optimization.
stocks.marketBelieves: Market sees KTB as a structurally better bank than in the past, with digital reach, improving ROE and strong asset quality.
stocks.marketMissing: Market may underappreciate monetization of Paotang/public payment rails and fee mix, but may also over-extrapolate recent re-rating.
stocks.variables: NIM, fee growth, cost/income, NPL, coverage, credit cost, ROE, dividend payout, digital active users.
stocks.fit: Income/quality bank investor; suitable for investors comfortable with policy linkage and moderate growth.
stocks.moatReason: Government ecosystem, Paotang/Krungthai NEXT scale, distribution, deposits and high regulatory barriers create durable customer access and data advantages.
stocks.industryComparison: เทียบกับ Large Thai Banks ด้วย ROE, NIM, NPL, Coverage, CAR, Cost/Income และ P/BV เท่านั้น.

stocks.debtEbitdaNote: Approx. net debt/EBITDA = (SET EV - Market Cap) / SET EBITDA = ~0.50x.
stocks.summary: ธุรกิจแข็งแรงและงบดุลดีมาก กำไร 1H26 ได้ทั้ง Volume และ Price หนุน แต่ต้องแยก 'คุณภาพบริษัท' ออกจาก 'ราคาน้ำมันที่สูงผิดปกติ' เวลาประเมินมูลค่า.

framework.1. Management: PTT holds 63.79%, giving strategic alignment with Thailand energy security. CEO Montri Rawanchaikul has E&P technical background and has led production ramp-up plus Malaysia expansion. Management track record is disciplined on upstream execution and dividends; state-linked strategic objectives remain part of the mandate.
framework.2. Product / Moat: Core upstream oil & gas E&P. Moat: มี — reserves/resources, operating licenses, geological/engineering know-how, scale, long-cycle project capability and access to strategic acreage. Durability high but economics remain commodity-price dependent.
framework.3. TAM / Growth Runway: Runway comes from Thailand gas production, Malaysia and acquired assets. Five-year investment plan 2026-30 is USD33.3bn; company targets volume growth through project development and M&A. TAM is global upstream energy, but capital intensity is high.
framework.4. Positive Catalysts: High oil/gas prices; volume growth; SK405B first oil targeted 2028; Malaysia portfolio expansion; new discoveries/M&A; dividends. Near-term oil catalyst high impact but externally driven; project catalysts medium/high over 1-5 years.
framework.5. Competitors: Compare with regional/global E&P peers on reserve life, production growth, unit cost, realized price, FCF, net debt and EV/EBITDA. Competitive edge is Thailand/Malaysia resource position and strong balance sheet.
framework.6. Revenue Growth & Margin: 1H26 revenue THB176.8bn, sales volume +14% YoY and ASP +10%; operating leverage to commodity prices is strong. Margin expansion is mostly price/mix/volume-driven; cost discipline and reuse initiatives help capex efficiency.
framework.7. Regulation: Petroleum concessions/PSC, royalties, taxes, decommissioning and environmental regulation are central. Regulation is both barrier to entry and cash-flow burden; host-country terms can materially change project NPV.
framework.8. Narrative & Sentiment: Narrative currently benefits from energy security and high oil prices. Sentiment positive, but part of the story is cyclical. With Brent above US$100 amid Middle East disruption, market is pricing a stronger commodity backdrop.
framework.9. Valuation Effect: 8.4x P/E and 2.8x EV/EBITDA look low, but normalized valuation should assume lower long-term oil. Multiple expansion is possible only if production growth raises normalized FCF rather than relying on spot oil.
framework.10. Earnings & Macro: 1H26 NPAT THB39.0bn vs ~THB30.1bn prior year; revenue THB176.8bn; volume 563k BOED. Base: oil normalizes but volume grows; Bull: sustained high oil + project execution; Bear: oil normalization + cost/capex slippage.
framework.11. Risk Radar: Top risks: oil/gas price (high/high), geopolitics (medium/high), project execution/reserves (medium/high), host-country regulation/tax (medium/medium), energy transition (low-medium/long-term high). Monitor Brent, gas prices, sales volume, unit cost, reserve replacement and capex.

stocks.thesis: Strong upstream franchise, low leverage, dividend capacity and visible production growth provide a robust base even if commodity prices normalize.
stocks.bear: Current oil prices are unusually elevated; earnings and valuation can look optically cheap near the top of a commodity cycle. Exploration/project misses can erode reserve replacement.
stocks.marketBelieves: Market sees PTTEP as a high-quality oil/gas proxy with strong dividends and direct benefit from energy tightness.
stocks.marketMissing: Market may underprice the durability of Malaysia/Thailand production growth, but may overprice the persistence of current oil prices.
stocks.variables: Brent/Dubai, realized price, sales volume, unit cost, reserve replacement, capex, new project FID/COD, net debt, dividend.
stocks.fit: Commodity/dividend investor seeking strong balance sheet; must tolerate oil-price volatility.
stocks.moatReason: Resource access, licenses, subsurface/engineering expertise, project scale and strategic domestic position create high entry barriers; commodity exposure limits pricing power.
stocks.industryComparison: เทียบกับ E&P peers ด้วย Production Growth, Reserve Life, Unit Cost, FCF, Net Debt, EV/EBITDA และ Dividend.

stocks.debtEbitdaNote: Use NIM, NPL, Coverage, CAR and ROE instead of Debt/EBITDA.
stocks.summary: ภาพรวมคือ 'คุณภาพดีขึ้น แต่ไม่ใช่ Growth Bank' — ผลตอบแทนระยะต่อไปขึ้นกับ Fee/Wealth/Productivity และการคุม Credit Cost มากกว่าการเร่งสินเชื่อ.

framework.1. Management: CEO Kattiya Indaravijaya has led a quality-over-volume strategy focused on customer economics, productivity and prudent credit. Ownership is widely held/free-float high, reducing controlling-shareholder risk. Capital allocation prioritizes capital strength and risk-adjusted returns.
framework.2. Product / Moat: Universal bank with strong SME/corporate/retail, K PLUS, wealth, payments and regional network. Moat: มี — customer data, K PLUS ecosystem, deposit franchise, SME relationships, brand and regulatory barriers. Durability high if digital engagement translates into fee income and risk selection.
framework.3. TAM / Growth Runway: Thai loan TAM is mature; growth runway comes from wealth, payments, cross-border, digital engagement and selective secured/high-quality lending. 2026 loan target only 0-2%, signaling value over volume.
framework.4. Positive Catalysts: Wealth fee growth; productivity/AI; lower operating cost; quality lending; capital return; asset-quality improvement. Probability high / impact medium over 6-24 months.
framework.5. Competitors: Industry comparison only with Thai large banks on NIM, ROE, NPL, coverage, CAR, fee growth and P/BV. KBank's strengths are digital/SME/customer analytics; risk is SME/retail credit sensitivity.
framework.6. Revenue Growth & Margin: 1H26 NPAT THB27.9bn +6.2% YoY; underlying ex-one-off growth only ~1.3%. NIM fell to 2.91% but non-interest income and lower opex offset pressure. Margin story is productivity + fees rather than NIM expansion.
framework.7. Regulation: BOT capital, responsible lending, cyber/data/privacy and consumer rules are key. Regulation raises fixed costs and constrains loan pricing but protects incumbents and deposit confidence.
framework.8. Narrative & Sentiment: Narrative is 'high-quality digital bank + improving efficiency' rather than aggressive loan growth. Sentiment positive/neutral; story is middle stage and increasingly depends on sustainable ROE.
framework.9. Valuation Effect: 235 baht, ~10.8x P/E, ~0.96x P/BV. Around book value is reasonable for ~9-10% ROE; meaningful re-rating requires sustained ROE above cost of equity and stable asset quality.
framework.10. Earnings & Macro: 1H26 NPAT THB27.9bn, NIM 2.91%, NPL 3.18%, coverage 173.9%, CAR 19.24%, ROE 9.65%. Base: stable profit with NIM pressure; Bull: wealth/fees/productivity; Bear: credit cost/NIM deterioration.
framework.11. Risk Radar: Top risks: NIM compression (high/medium), SME/retail asset quality (medium/high), weak domestic growth (medium/high), cyber/digital risk (low-medium/high), fee-market sensitivity (medium/medium). Monitor NIM, NPL, credit cost, coverage, fee income, ROE, CAR.

stocks.thesis: Strong digital/customer franchise, high capital and disciplined risk management give resilience; current valuation is reasonable for a quality bank.
stocks.bear: Underlying profit growth is modest after stripping one-off income; weak economy and rate cuts can limit ROE improvement, especially if SME credit worsens.
stocks.marketBelieves: Market sees KBank as a digital leader with improving cost efficiency and strong capital, but still exposed to Thailand/SME cycle.
stocks.marketMissing: Market may underappreciate long-term wealth/payment monetization and AI productivity, while underestimating NIM and SME-credit drag.
stocks.variables: NIM, credit cost, NPL, coverage, ROE, CAR, fee/wealth income, loan mix, K PLUS engagement.
stocks.fit: Core bank investor seeking digital franchise + capital strength; moderate cyclical risk.
stocks.moatReason: K PLUS/customer data, SME relationships, deposit franchise, brand and regulation produce durable switching/data/distribution advantages.
stocks.industryComparison: เทียบกับ Large Thai Banks ด้วย ROE, NIM, NPL, Coverage, CAR, Fee Growth, Cost/Income และ P/BV.

stocks.summary: ฐานธนาคารยังแข็งแรง แต่กำไร 1H26 ลดจากดอกเบี้ยขาลง จุดชี้ขาดคือ Wealth/Fees และ Gen2-Gen3 จะสร้าง ROE เพิ่มได้จริงหรือไม่.

framework.1. Management: SCBX is led by CEO Arthid Nanthawithaya; group structure separates core bank, consumer/digital finance and technology/platform businesses. Management has demonstrated cost discipline and active portfolio redesign, but returns from Gen2/Gen3 remain the key proof point.
framework.2. Product / Moat: Core bank plus CardX, AutoX, InnovestX, SCB 10X, DataX/TechX and BankX optionality. Moat: มี — large customer/deposit base, wealth franchise, data/technology assets and regulatory barriers. Durability high in core bank; digital moat still developing.
framework.3. TAM / Growth Runway: Core banking TAM is mature. Growth runway comes from wealth, fee income, consumer finance normalization and Gen3/BankX technology businesses. BankX can widen addressable digital-finance markets but execution risk is meaningful.
framework.4. Positive Catalysts: Wealth fees; trading/investment income normalization; cost control; CardX/AutoX credit normalization; BankX launch/AI capabilities; capital return. Timeline 6-36 months.
framework.5. Competitors: Industry comparison only with Thai large banks on ROE/NIM/NPL/CAR/PBV, while digital subsidiaries should be judged on profitability, CAC, credit loss and unit economics rather than hype.
framework.6. Revenue Growth & Margin: 2Q26 fee income +14.8% YoY and opex -2.2% helped offset NIM pressure. Margin expansion depends on mix shift toward fee/wealth and better Gen2 economics; core NIM remains pressured by low rates.
framework.7. Regulation: BOT consolidated supervision, capital rules, digital banking approvals, responsible lending, data privacy and cyber regulation are central. Regulation is barrier to entry but can slow innovation/monetization.
framework.8. Narrative & Sentiment: Narrative is 'bank cash cow funding digital optionality'. Sentiment neutral-positive; market gives some credit for optionality but still values SCB mainly as a bank/dividend stock. Story is middle stage.
framework.9. Valuation Effect: At ~1.02x P/BV and 11.3x P/E, valuation is fair for current ROE/profit trend. Re-rating needs visible Gen2/Gen3 profit contribution or stronger sustainable fee growth.
framework.10. Earnings & Macro: 2Q26 NPAT THB11.1bn, +9% QoQ but -13.1% YoY; 1H26 NPAT THB21.3bn vs THB25.3bn. NPL 3.17%, coverage 158.6%, CAR 18.6%. Base: resilient but slower; Bull: digital/fee upside; Bear: NIM+credit pressure.
framework.11. Risk Radar: Top risks: NIM compression (high/medium), consumer finance credit losses (medium/high), execution of BankX/digital portfolio (medium/high), macro/household debt (medium/high), regulatory change (medium/medium).

stocks.thesis: Core SCB franchise generates cash and capital while wealth/digital initiatives provide optionality; downside is cushioned by capital strength and diversified income.
stocks.bear: Gen2/Gen3 may continue consuming capital without sufficient ROE; falling rates pressure the core earnings engine before new businesses become material.
stocks.marketBelieves: Market believes SCBX is a mature bank with attractive dividend plus some fintech optionality, but not yet a proven high-growth tech platform.
stocks.marketMissing: Market may be missing upside from AI/wealth/BankX if unit economics improve, or may be too generous about timing of digital profitability.
stocks.variables: NIM, fee/wealth income, Gen2 credit cost, NPL/coverage, CAR, BankX milestones, cost/income, dividend payout.
stocks.fit: Income/value bank investor who wants digital optionality but accepts execution risk.
stocks.moatReason: Large customer/deposit base, wealth franchise, data/technology stack and banking regulation create durable core-bank moat; digital moat is not yet fully proven.
stocks.industryComparison: เทียบกับ Large Thai Banks ด้วย ROE, NIM, NPL, Coverage, CAR, Cost/Income, P/BV; digital businessesดู Unit Economics แยก.

stocks.summary: TRUE เปลี่ยนจาก 'เรื่องควบรวม' เป็น 'เรื่อง Margin + FCF + Deleveraging' แล้ว จุดสำคัญคือรายได้โตไม่มาก แต่ EBITDA โตแรงจาก Synergy; ราคาปัจจุบันต้องการให้การปรับดีขึ้นดำเนินต่อ.

framework.1. Management: Post-merger management has focused on synergy capture, network modernization, cost discipline and deleveraging. Execution has improved materially since 2023. Strategic alignment benefits from large CP Group/Telenor ecosystems, though ownership concentration and capital-intensity require governance monitoring.
framework.2. Product / Moat: Mobile, broadband, enterprise, TV/content and digital services. Moat: มี — spectrum, nationwide network, subscriber scale, distribution, converged services and high capex/regulatory barriers. Durability high if network quality and pricing discipline are sustained.
framework.3. TAM / Growth Runway: Thai mobile is mature, but growth runway exists in ARPU, 5G monetization, broadband, enterprise/cloud, data/AI services and cross-sell. Biggest value driver is not TAM expansion alone but post-merger unit-economics improvement.
framework.4. Positive Catalysts: Synergy realization; network opex/capex efficiency; ARPU/pricing discipline; deleveraging; lower finance cost; enterprise/cloud/AI; dividends. Probability high / impact high over 6-24 months.
framework.5. Competitors: Industry comparison with Thai telecom only: ARPU, churn, service revenue growth, EBITDA margin, capex/sales, spectrum cost, FCF and leverage. TRUE's scale/convergence is strong; balance sheet remains weaker than ideal.
framework.6. Revenue Growth & Margin: Q2 service revenue +0.8% YoY while EBITDA +13.5% demonstrates operating leverage. Margin expansion comes from synergy, network consolidation, opex reduction and mix; leverage fell to ~3.7x.
framework.7. Regulation: NBTC spectrum, pricing/competition, service quality, data privacy and telecom infrastructure rules are key. Regulation is a high barrier but spectrum obligations and policy intervention affect cash flow.
framework.8. Narrative & Sentiment: Narrative is 'turnaround to cash-flow compounder' rather than merger clean-up. Sentiment positive but expectations now include continuing synergy and deleveraging. Story is middle stage, not early.
framework.9. Valuation Effect: P/E 23.4x and P/BV 5.5x appear high; EV/EBITDA 7.8x is more relevant. Fair value requires continued EBITDA/FCF growth and falling leverage. Multiple expansion is less likely than earnings-driven return.
framework.10. Earnings & Macro: Q2 reported NPAT ~THB6.6bn, service revenue ~THB41.4bn +0.8% YoY, EBITDA +13.5%, capex ~THB4.6bn, leverage 3.7x. Base: synergy + modest revenue growth; Bull: ARPU/enterprise upside; Bear: price war/spectrum/capex.
framework.11. Risk Radar: Top risks: leverage/refinancing (medium/high), renewed price competition (medium/high), spectrum/capex burden (medium/high), regulation (medium/medium), execution of synergy/network quality (medium/high). Monitor ARPU, churn, service revenue, EBITDA margin, capex, FCF, leverage and interest cost.

stocks.thesis: Merger synergies are now visible in EBITDA and profit; network scale and convergence create durable competitive economics if pricing remains rational.
stocks.bear: Valuation already anticipates successful synergy and deleveraging. Revenue growth remains modest, leverage is still material, and renewed competition could reverse margin progress.
stocks.marketBelieves: Market believes TRUE has passed the merger pain point and is becoming a higher-margin, cash-generative telecom with improving leverage.
stocks.marketMissing: Market may underestimate additional synergy/AI efficiency and enterprise monetization, but may also underestimate spectrum/refinancing and competitive risk.
stocks.variables: Mobile ARPU, subscribers/churn, broadband revenue, EBITDA margin, capex, FCF, net debt/EBITDA, financing cost, spectrum payments.
stocks.fit: Turnaround/growth investor comfortable with leverage and execution risk; also increasingly relevant to credit investors as leverage falls.
stocks.moatReason: Spectrum, nationwide network, subscriber scale, convergence, distribution and regulatory/capital barriers create a durable telecom moat.
stocks.industryComparison: เทียบกับ Telecom peers ด้วย ARPU, Churn, Service Revenue Growth, EBITDA Margin, Capex/Sales, FCF, Spectrum Cost และ Leverage.

stocks.debtEbitdaNote: CPALL One Report 2024 reported Net Debt/EBITDA 3.0x; use as reference only until current-quarter leverage is sourced.
stocks.summary: CPALL ยังมี Moat แข็งมากจาก Density + Logistics + Daily Habit. จุดชี้ขาดไม่ใช่จำนวนร้านอย่างเดียว แต่คือ SSSG, Margin และ Deleveraging; valuation ปัจจุบันไม่ตึงเท่าอดีต.

framework.1. Management: CP Group-linked retail platform with long operating history and strong execution in convenience retail. Management has consistently expanded store density, fresh-food mix, digital payments and supply-chain efficiency; capital allocation became more leveraged after CPAXT-related transactions, so deleveraging discipline remains an important shareholder-alignment test.
framework.2. Product / Moat: 7-Eleven Thailand plus support businesses and investment exposure to wholesale/retail. Moat: มี — unmatched store density, brand, daily-use habit, purchasing scale, logistics, distribution, data and franchise ecosystem. Durability high because replication requires nationwide sites, logistics and supplier economics.
framework.3. TAM / Growth Runway: Thailand convenience retail is mature but still offers runway through store additions, higher sales/store, fresh food, ready-to-eat, delivery, health/beauty and digital services. Growth is more about wallet share and density economics than greenfield TAM.
framework.4. Positive Catalysts: Same-store sales recovery; higher gross margin mix; private label/fresh food; operating leverage; interest-cost reduction; debt paydown; CPAXT value recovery. Probability medium-high / impact medium-high over 6-24 months.
framework.5. Competitors: Industry comparison only with food/convenience retail on SSSG, sales/sqm, gross margin, store productivity, inventory turns, FCF, leverage and EV/EBITDA. CPALL's density/logistics advantage is structurally stronger than ordinary retailers.
framework.6. Revenue Growth & Margin: Q2/26 NPAT THB7.51bn +11% YoY; 1H26 THB16.63bn +15.9%. Earnings growth is faster than topline due mix, scale and operating leverage. Further margin expansion depends on fresh-food mix, cost control and funding cost.
framework.7. Regulation: Retail zoning, food safety, labor, competition, consumer/data privacy and payment regulation matter. Regulation is mostly cost/compliance risk rather than moat, but nationwide operating scale helps absorb fixed compliance cost.
framework.8. Narrative & Sentiment: Narrative is 'defensive compounder at de-rated valuation'. Sentiment is more cautious than in past growth phases because leverage and consumer softness have reduced the old premium. Story is middle-stage recovery rather than early growth.
framework.9. Valuation Effect: At ~12.4x P/E and 10.4x EV/EBITDA, valuation is below the premium historically associated with CPALL. Multiple expansion is possible if leverage and SSSG improve, but earnings growth should remain the primary return driver.
framework.10. Earnings & Macro: 1H26 NPAT THB16.63bn vs THB14.35bn. Base: moderate SSSG + margin/interest-cost improvement; Bull: consumption recovery + stronger fresh-food mix; Bear: weak consumption + leverage/funding pressure. 3-5y case depends on store economics and deleveraging.
framework.11. Risk Radar: Top risks: household spending (medium/high), leverage/refinancing (medium/high), wage/opex inflation (medium/medium), CPAXT execution (medium/high), regulatory/competition pressure (low-medium/medium). Monitor SSSG, gross margin, FCF, net debt, interest expense and store productivity.

stocks.thesis: Dominant convenience-store moat, recurring daily demand and improving earnings quality provide a strong long-term compounding base, while current valuation is less demanding than historical premium levels.
stocks.bear: High leverage and exposure to Thai consumption can keep valuation depressed; if SSSG slows, fixed-cost leverage can work in reverse and debt reduction may take longer.
stocks.marketBelieves: Market believes CPALL remains the dominant Thai convenience retailer but deserves a lower multiple because of leverage and slower consumer growth.
stocks.marketMissing: Market may be underpricing margin mix, fresh-food economics and balance-sheet repair if earnings compound faster than revenue.
stocks.variables: SSSG, gross margin, new stores, basket size, fresh-food mix, FCF, net debt/EBITDA, interest cost, CPAXT earnings.
stocks.fit: Core compounder / defensive growth investor who accepts leverage but wants recurring consumer demand.
stocks.moatReason: Store density, 7-Eleven brand, purchasing power, logistics, data and customer habit form a network/scale moat that is difficult and expensive to replicate.
stocks.industryComparison: เทียบกับ Convenience/Food Retail peers ด้วย SSSG, Sales/Store, Gross Margin, Inventory Turns, FCF, Leverage และ EV/EBITDA.

stocks.debtEbitdaNote: Use capital adequacy, NPL, coverage, NIM and ROE rather than Debt/EBITDA.
stocks.summary: BBL คือ 'Balance Sheet ก่อน Growth' — ถูกบน P/BV แต่ catalyst ต้องมาจาก ROE/fee/corporate loan และ dividend ไม่ใช่แค่หวัง multiple re-rate.

framework.1. Management: Family-influenced but professionally managed bank with long conservative underwriting culture and the largest overseas network among Thai banks. Management historically prioritizes capital strength, liquidity and corporate-banking relationships over aggressive short-term ROE maximization.
framework.2. Product / Moat: Corporate/SME/retail banking plus ASEAN/international network. Moat: มี — large low-cost deposit base, blue-chip corporate relationships, cross-border network, balance-sheet scale and regulatory barriers. Durability high, though digital retail advantage is less distinctive than some peers.
framework.3. TAM / Growth Runway: Thai banking TAM is mature; growth runway is cross-border corporate banking, ASEAN trade/investment, wealth and fee income. Loan growth is less important than maintaining spreads and credit quality through cycles.
framework.4. Positive Catalysts: Fee recovery; corporate/FDI loan demand; ASEAN trade finance; benign credit cost; capital return/dividend; potential re-rating from deep P/BV discount. Timeline 6-24 months.
framework.5. Competitors: Compare only with large banks on ROE, NIM, CET1/CAR, NPL, coverage, fee income and P/BV. BBL's edge is corporate/international franchise and capital buffer; weakness is lower structural ROE and retail-digital monetization.
framework.6. Revenue Growth & Margin: 1H26 NPAT THB20.49bn, down 16.2% YoY as lower rates pressure net interest income. Earnings resilience comes from fee income, treasury and conservative provisioning. Margin expansion is unlikely near term; efficiency and lower credit cost are more relevant.
framework.7. Regulation: BOT capital/liquidity, responsible lending, cross-border regulation, AML and data/cyber requirements are core. High regulation protects incumbent funding franchises but caps leverage and raises compliance cost.
framework.8. Narrative & Sentiment: Narrative is 'deep-value, well-capitalized regional bank'. Sentiment neutral-positive because valuation is low, but earnings momentum is softer in a rate-cut cycle. Story is mature/value rather than growth.
framework.9. Valuation Effect: At ~8.3x P/E and ~0.6x P/BV, valuation is cheap on assets. Re-rating requires sustainable ROE despite lower NIM; dividends and retained book-value growth are central to expected return.
framework.10. Earnings & Macro: 1H26 NPAT THB20.49bn vs THB24.46bn; Q2 THB9.50bn. Base: lower NIM but stable asset quality; Bull: fee/loan recovery + benign credit cost; Bear: NIM compression + corporate/NPL deterioration.
framework.11. Risk Radar: Top risks: NIM compression (high/medium), corporate/SME credit cycle (medium/high), overseas/geopolitical exposure (medium/medium), weak domestic loan demand (medium/medium), cyber/regulatory risk (low-medium/high). Monitor NIM, NPL, coverage, CAR/CET1, ROE, fee income and dividend.

stocks.thesis: Deep discount to book plus strong capital and corporate/ASEAN franchise create a favorable margin of safety for value/income investors.
stocks.bear: Low P/BV can remain low if sustainable ROE stays below cost of equity; rate cuts and weak loan demand can delay re-rating.
stocks.marketBelieves: Market sees BBL as the conservative, well-capitalized Thai bank with lower growth but high balance-sheet resilience.
stocks.marketMissing: Market may underappreciate ASEAN/corporate franchise optionality and capital return, while correctly discounting structurally lower ROE.
stocks.variables: NIM, loan growth, fee income, NPL, credit cost, coverage, CET1/CAR, ROE, dividend payout.
stocks.fit: Value/income bank investor prioritizing capital strength over growth.
stocks.moatReason: Corporate relationships, deposit base, ASEAN network, balance-sheet scale and banking regulation create durable funding/distribution barriers.
stocks.industryComparison: เทียบกับ Large Thai Banks ด้วย ROE, NIM, NPL, Coverage, CET1/CAR, Fee Income และ P/BV; Debt/EBITDA = N/A.

stocks.debtEbitdaNote: Approx. gross debt/EBITDA screening = (EV-MCap+cash proxy unavailable); leverage remains elevated, so treat 7.6x as conservative screening estimate, not reported covenant ratio.
stocks.summary: SCC ตอนนี้ต้องอ่านเป็น 'Recovery + Balance Sheet Repair' มากกว่า Quality Compounder แบบอดีต จุดชี้ขาดคือ Chemicals/LSP และการลดหนี้ ไม่ใช่กำไร headline ที่มี one-off.

framework.1. Management: Long-standing industrial holding company with broad operating expertise across cement, chemicals, packaging and distribution. Management has strong project/engineering track record, but recent large-cycle investments raised balance-sheet and capital-allocation scrutiny; asset sales and portfolio discipline are now key.
framework.2. Product / Moat: Holding company spanning cement/green solutions, smart living/distribution, chemicals, SCGP and SCGD. Moat: มี — brands, distribution, industrial sites, technology/process know-how, scale and ecosystem relationships. Durability varies by segment; chemicals has weaker pricing power than cement/distribution.
framework.3. TAM / Growth Runway: TAM spans ASEAN construction, packaging and petrochemicals. Growth runway comes from regional demand recovery, LSP normalization, high-value-added products, low-carbon cement, packaging and portfolio reshaping rather than one single high-growth market.
framework.4. Positive Catalysts: Petrochemical cycle recovery; LSP utilization improvement; asset monetization; Chandra Asri transaction proceeds; cement demand/pricing; cost reduction; deleveraging. Probability mixed / impact high over 6-36 months.
framework.5. Competitors: Use segment-specific industry peers: cement on volume/price/energy cost/EBITDA; chemicals on spreads/utilization; packaging on volume/margin. Group valuation should use SOTP and leverage, not a single P/E.
framework.6. Revenue Growth & Margin: Q2/26 reported NPAT THB11.5bn, but headline profit contains transaction/asset effects; normalized earnings are the key signal. Margin recovery depends on chemical spreads, LSP utilization, energy costs and cost reduction.
framework.7. Regulation: Environmental/carbon regulation, industrial permits, energy policy, competition and cross-border investment rules are material. Carbon rules are both risk and opportunity because SCG can monetize low-carbon products if transition investment earns adequate ROIC.
framework.8. Narrative & Sentiment: Narrative shifted from 'quality conglomerate' to 'recovery + balance-sheet repair'. Sentiment improved after asset transactions and better normalized earnings, but chemicals remain the central debate. Story is middle-cycle recovery.
framework.9. Valuation Effect: P/BV ~0.88x provides asset support, while P/E is less useful due cyclical/one-off earnings. SOTP suggests upside if chemicals normalize and debt falls; multiple expansion is conditional on ROIC recovery.
framework.10. Earnings & Macro: 1H26 NPAT THB17.76bn vs THB18.44bn. Base: gradual chemicals/cement recovery; Bull: spreads + LSP + deleveraging; Bear: prolonged petrochemical oversupply and weak ASEAN demand. 3-5y upside depends on normalized ROIC of major assets.
framework.11. Risk Radar: Top risks: petrochemical oversupply (high/high), leverage/refinancing (medium-high/high), LSP execution (medium/high), weak construction demand (medium/medium), energy/carbon cost (medium/medium). Monitor spreads, LSP utilization, net debt, EBITDA, FCF, cement price and asset sales.

stocks.thesis: Asset base, brands and industrial know-how remain valuable; recovery and deleveraging can unlock value from a sub-book valuation.
stocks.bear: Chemicals can stay structurally oversupplied for years; high capital intensity and leverage can destroy value even if headline asset value looks cheap.
stocks.marketBelieves: Market believes SCC is in a cyclical recovery and deleveraging phase, with asset sales reducing balance-sheet stress.
stocks.marketMissing: Market may underestimate how long petrochemical oversupply can persist, or conversely the earnings torque if LSP and spreads normalize together.
stocks.variables: Chemical spreads, LSP run rate, cement price/volume, SCGP margins, net debt, interest cost, asset monetization, FCF.
stocks.fit: Deep-value/cyclical investor comfortable with conglomerate complexity and commodity risk.
stocks.moatReason: Industrial scale, brands, distribution, sites and operating know-how form a moat, but moat strength differs by segment and is weakest in commodity chemicals.
stocks.industryComparison: เทียบแยก Segment: Cement, Chemicals, Packaging; ระดับ Group ใช้ SOTP, ROIC, Net Debt/EBITDA และ FCF.

stocks.debtEbitdaNote: Latest easily verifiable company reference shows Net Debt/EBITDA around 0.5x; leverage policy ceiling 2.5x.
stocks.summary: BDMS Business Quality ยังสูงมาก แต่ 1H26 แสดงชัดว่า Moat ไม่ได้แปลว่ากำไรต้องโตทุกไตรมาส ตอนนี้ต้องรอ Patient Mix/International/Margin กลับมาเร่งอีกครั้ง.

framework.1. Management: Founder/family-linked healthcare platform with professional management and long record of network expansion, clinical investment and disciplined capital structure. Governance benefits from strong medical/operational expertise and conservative leverage.
framework.2. Product / Moat: 50+ hospitals across Thailand/Cambodia under Bangkok Hospital, Samitivej, BNH, Phyathai, Paolo and Royal brands plus labs/pharma support. Moat: มี — doctor network, clinical reputation, referral network, geographic density, brand, high fixed investment and licenses. Durability very high.
framework.3. TAM / Growth Runway: Thailand private healthcare TAM grows with aging, chronic disease, higher income, insurance penetration and medical tourism. BDMS can grow via complex-care mix, international patients, wellness/prevention and network utilization rather than hospital count alone.
framework.4. Positive Catalysts: International patient recovery; Middle East/CLMV medical tourism; complex-care mix; utilization; pricing; wellness/prevention; operating leverage; dividends. Probability medium-high / impact medium-high over 6-36 months.
framework.5. Competitors: Compare with hospital peers on patient volume, revenue/intensity, EBITDA margin, ROIC, international mix, doctor network, capex and EV/EBITDA. BDMS has exceptional scale/network breadth.
framework.6. Revenue Growth & Margin: 6M26 operating income THB56.1bn vs THB55.6bn, but NPAT THB7.31bn fell 6.8% YoY and EBITDA margin eased to 23.3%. Growth is currently volume/mix constrained; margin expansion requires higher international/complex-care mix and utilization.
framework.7. Regulation: Hospital licensing, professional standards, insurance/copayment rules, pricing transparency, data privacy and foreign-patient policy matter. Regulation raises entry barriers but can affect reimbursement and patient behavior.
framework.8. Narrative & Sentiment: Narrative is 'defensive healthcare compounder with medical-tourism moat'. Sentiment neutral because business quality remains high while near-term earnings growth slowed. Story is mature compounder, not early-cycle.
framework.9. Valuation Effect: At ~19.7x P/E and ~12.2x EV/EBITDA, valuation is fair-to-premium versus market but supported by superior moat and balance sheet. Re-rating needs earnings growth to reaccelerate; compression risk exists if margins stay soft.
framework.10. Earnings & Macro: 6M26 NPAT THB7.31bn vs THB7.84bn; Q2 THB3.25bn. Base: gradual patient/mix recovery; Bull: international + complex-care growth; Bear: weak Thai demand/copayment effects + wage/doctor cost. Long term remains tied to aging and medical tourism.
framework.11. Risk Radar: Top risks: patient volume/mix (medium/high), medical inflation/staff cost (medium/medium), insurance/copayment policy (medium/medium), medical-tourism shocks (low-medium/high), execution of new services/capex (low-medium/medium).

stocks.thesis: One of the strongest service moats in Thailand: network, doctors, referral density, trusted brands and conservative leverage support durable compounding.
stocks.bear: Premium valuation can de-rate if earnings remain flat; domestic affordability and insurance changes can slow volume while staff costs remain sticky.
stocks.marketBelieves: Market believes BDMS deserves a premium for defensive growth, network moat and medical tourism exposure.
stocks.marketMissing: Market may underappreciate long-term complex-care/wellness monetization, but near-term margin recovery could take longer than expected.
stocks.variables: Thai/international patient revenue, intensity per visit, EBITDA margin, occupancy/utilization, doctor cost, capex, ROIC, net debt, dividend.
stocks.fit: Quality/defensive growth investor willing to pay a premium for durable healthcare moat.
stocks.moatReason: Clinical reputation, doctor/referral network, hospital density, brand and licensing form a durable healthcare network moat.
stocks.industryComparison: เทียบกับ Hospital peers ด้วย Revenue Growth, EBITDA Margin, International Mix, ROIC, Capex, Occupancy/Utilization และ EV/EBITDA.

stocks.debtEbitdaNote: Total Interest Bearing Debt / EBITDA, 6M/2026, TTM-adjusted by SET.
stocks.summary: CPN มี Moat ชัดจาก Location + Tenant Ecosystem + Development Scale. Q2/26 ยังทำ record rental revenue; สิ่งที่ต้องเฝ้าคือ Capex/ROIC ของโครงการใหม่และ Debt/EBITDA.

framework.1. Management: Central Group-linked property platform with long track record in mall development, tenant management and mixed-use execution. Management has consistently recycled capital, expanded recurring rental income and maintained disciplined project pipeline.
framework.2. Product / Moat: 45 shopping centers plus community malls, offices, hotels and residential projects. Moat: มี — prime locations, tenant ecosystem, traffic data, brand, scale, development capability and network effects between malls/retailers. Durability high because prime sites are scarce and tenant economics favor high-traffic platforms.
framework.3. TAM / Growth Runway: Thailand retail-property TAM grows through urbanization, tourism, premium mixed-use and regional city consumption. Runway comes from new malls, asset enhancement, hotels, residential and mixed-use ecosystems.
framework.4. Positive Catalysts: New/ramped malls; record rental revenue; tenant sales/traffic; mixed-use launches; hotel expansion; residential transfers; efficiency; potential CPNREIT monetization. Probability high / impact medium-high over 6-36 months.
framework.5. Competitors: Compare with mall/property peers on occupancy, rental growth, tenant sales, EBITDA margin, FFO/CF, debt/EBITDA, NAV and ROIC. CPN's mall platform has stronger recurring economics than typical residential developers.
framework.6. Revenue Growth & Margin: Q2/26 revenue THB13.1bn +8% YoY and NPAT THB4.75bn +10%. Rental revenue hit another record; rental business was ~88% of total revenue incl. other income. Operating leverage benefits from occupancy and asset ramp-up.
framework.7. Regulation: Zoning, building permits, REIT rules, property tax, environmental requirements and consumer/tenant regulation matter. Entry barriers are high because prime land, permits, financing and tenant relationships are difficult to replicate.
framework.8. Narrative & Sentiment: Narrative is 'recurring-income compounder + mixed-use growth'. Sentiment positive/steady; market recognizes quality, so execution of new projects and rental growth must sustain the premium.
framework.9. Valuation Effect: At ~14x P/E and ~10.7x EV/EBITDA, valuation is fair for a high-quality recurring-income property platform. Multiple expansion is possible but less important than rental/FFO growth and NAV creation.
framework.10. Earnings & Macro: 1H26 NPAT THB9.72bn +13.9% YoY; Q2 NPAT THB4.75bn +10%. Base: rental growth + project ramp-up; Bull: stronger traffic/tenant sales + asset monetization; Bear: consumption slowdown + capex/interest burden.
framework.11. Risk Radar: Top risks: consumer/tourism slowdown (medium/high), large capex pipeline (medium/high), interest rates/refinancing (medium/medium), project execution (medium/high), property cycle/competition (medium/medium). Monitor occupancy, rental growth, tenant sales, EBITDA margin, debt/EBITDA, capex and project openings.

stocks.thesis: Scarce prime locations, tenant network and recurring rental economics support durable growth; mixed-use expansion adds optionality.
stocks.bear: Large multi-year capex can dilute ROIC if traffic/tenant productivity disappoints; premium quality does not eliminate property-cycle and funding risk.
stocks.marketBelieves: Market believes CPN is Thailand's premier mall/mixed-use platform with resilient recurring income and strong execution.
stocks.marketMissing: Market may underprice long-duration NAV creation from mixed-use ecosystems, but may underestimate capex intensity and execution risk.
